title: Prove the sharp component threshold for commutative right-vector targets
body:
Commutativity alone does not make the right-vector query cost equal to delta on invertible targets. This answers Open question 3 of #4276: over `F2^3`, the component target `(I, [[0,1],[1,1]], [[1,1],[1,0]])` costs **exactly 3**, with **delta 2**, even though free `GL2(F2)` maps are allowed anywhere.

The scoped proof is sharp: over `K^k`, for a finite field of size `q`, all invertible targets cost at most 2 when `k<=q`, while examples cost 3 with delta 2 for every `k>=q+1`. It proves the common-unit-pivot criterion and constructs a complete three-factor word for invertible targets over finite products of field K-algebras. The all-finite-field statement uses a written quadratic-extension argument. The software witnesses cover only the listed prime fields. Singular targets and general commutative algebras remain outside scope.

An independent literal BFS covers all 216 invertible `F2^3` targets: `(cost,delta,count)=(0,0,6),(1,1,54),(2,2,144),(3,2,12)`. All 4,752 paid and 1,296 free edges, 132 conjugations, 216 matrix witnesses and 13,824 arbitrary-input cases pass. A separate projective/explicit-word oracle agrees on every cost/delta record, checks 8 prime-field sharp witnesses, 512 F3 first-column triples and 2,550 literal upper words. Both Python 3.12 normal/optimized warning-strict commands freshly execute both algorithms and compare complete typed artifacts. Source-history/public-byte preflight and committed Git-free export pass with all 16 files unchanged. Separate AI proof/code/integration review found no correctness defect; witness-order notation and the normal warning flag were clarified before freezing. No independent human or formal-kernel acceptance is claimed.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/right-vector-commutative-products`. Only this isolated package is added.
